Check get_pricing × traffic_gb against the balance first. IMPORTANT: wait ~5 seconds after the purchase before sending the first r

tools.name: list_proxies
tools.description: All proxies of the account with remaining traffic and connection credentials.

tools.name: extend_proxy
tools.description: Adds prepaid GB to an existing proxy (same credentials keep working). Deducts balance.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Live used / remaining traffic for one proxy.

tools.name: set_rotation
tools.description: Switch between rotate-every-request (port 824) and sticky interval 1..120 minutes (port 10000).

tools.name: link_telegram
tools.description: Returns a short code the human sends to the ProxyCove Telegram bot (@ProxyCove_bot → "Link website account"). After linking, the human can manage the account and issue new API keys from the bot — a second way to keep access if the API key is lost. Code expires in 30 minutes.

tools.name: attach_recovery
tools.description: Attaches an email to the account so the human can log in on proxycove.com (via "Forgot password") and never lose the balance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, create_topup · Private data: create_account, buy_proxy, list_proxies, get_credentials, extend_proxy, link_telegram, attach_recovery · Public sink: create_account, get_account, attach_recovery.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, create_topup · Private data: create_account, buy_proxy, list_proxies, get_credentials, extend_proxy, link_telegram, attach_recovery · Public sink: create_account, get_account, attach_recovery

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
